key_insight: A smoothly blended modified Moving Reference Frame (mMRF) removes the artificial discontinuity at the rotating-stationary interface while preserving the low cost of partially rotating propeller simulations.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical CFD alternative for propeller-hull interaction studies where full sliding-interface motion is too expensive but classical MRF is too crude for self-propulsion predictions.
method: Scale the frame rotation rate with a spatial function that decays from 1 near the propeller to 0 at the interface.
Derive the governing equations for the blended rotating frame and implement them in the FreSCo+ RANS solver.
Verify the formulation with the analytical Taylor--Couette solution and apply it to open-water and ship self-propulsion cases.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports verification against Taylor--Couette and application to open-water propeller and Japan Bulk Carrier self-propulsion simulations, with mMRF matching key integral propulsion metrics while reducing local interface artifacts.
watch_item: The approach still relies on a user-defined blending region/function, so performance and smoothness may depend on how that transition is chosen.
paper_title: A Modified Moving Reference Frame Method for Propeller Resolution
